title: How Has Roman Concrete Lasted for Millennia? 1,900-Year-Old Latrine Offers Clues
summary: Researchers analyzed a 1900-year-old Roman latrine to understand why ancient Roman concrete has survived millennia while modern concrete deteriorates. The study found that Roman concrete contains volcanic ash and lime that create self-healing calcium deposits, allowing cracks to seal themselves over time.
problem_solved: Explains the mystery of why Roman concrete structures have endured for nearly two millennia while modern concrete typically fails within 50 years.
why_valuable: Provides insights for developing more durable and sustainable modern concrete that could reduce infrastructure maintenance costs and carbon emissions.
